questions.question: Discuss "Valediction: Forbidding Mourning" as a Metaphysical poem. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Use of elaborate metaphysical conceits (compass metaphor for lovers’ souls). Blending
  • intellect and emotion; logical argument supporting spiritual love. Paradox and subtle
  • reasoning; philosophical contemplation of love beyond physical separation. Dramatic,
  • conversational tone; compact, profound ideas. Unconventional imagery and scholarly
  • references; meditation on constancy, spirituality, and transcendent love. [CO1]

questions.question: How does Donne console his beloved in " Valediction: Forbidding Mourning"? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Theme of spiritual, enduring love · Parting to be accepted calmly · Comparison with the
  • quiet death of virtuous men · Rejects "tear-floods" and public grief · Contrast between dull
  • sublunary lovers and refined love · Gold beaten to airy thinness — expansion without
  • breaking · Compass conceit — unity despite distance · Physical separation cannot weaken
  • true love · Metaphysical features: conceit, wit, argument, logic · (CO1)

questions.question: In what ways does Shelley’s description of the skylark reflect Romantic ideals about nature, art, and imagination? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Celebration of nature’s purity, freedom, and joy (skylark as an ideal). Symbolizes
  • transcendent art, spiritual inspiration untouched by sorrow. Contrasts human struggles with
  • bird’s happiness; imagination as poetic creativity. Strong emotion and awe before nature;
  • pantheistic undertones. Vivid imagery and lyrical style; subjective experience and natural
  • beauty prioritized. [CO2]

questions.question: Discuss the blending of Romantic ideals with Gothic elements in "La Belle Dame Sans Merci". / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Medieval ballad setting and form · Knight meets a mysterious, beautiful lady · Romantic
  • celebration of beauty, imagination, the supernatural · Idyllic wooing — garland, bracelets,
  • elfin grot · Gothic elements: pale kings, death imagery, desolate landscape · Dream vision
  • reveals danger and betrayal · Themes of illusion, enchantment, fatal love · Sedge withered,
  • no birds sing — barrenness after enchantment · Ballad repetition and refrain heighten
  • dramatic effect · (CO2)

questions.solution_html:

  • of traditional silencing—poetic expression and agency. Metaphor and simile evoke Anne’s
  • memory and longing. Challenges patriarchal literary history, restoring woman’s perspective.

questions.question: In what ways does the poem "The Lake Isle of Innisfree" reflect Irish society's perspective on urbanization? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Desire to escape city life ("pavements grey") · Innisfree as symbol of peace and
  • simplicity · Self-sufficient rural life — cabin, bean-rows, hive · Nature offers spiritual and
  • emotional comfort · Contrast between urban noise and rural tranquillity · Irish landscape and
  • the Celtic Revival's national identity · Implicit critique of industrialisation and displacement ·
  • Rich natural imagery and musical rhythm · Peace attained through memory and imagination ·
  • (CO4)

questions.question: What information does the dramatic monologue "My Last Duchess" provide about the different characters in the poem. / [CO3] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Dramatic monologue reveals character indirectly · Duke: proud, possessive, authoritarian,
  • connoisseur of art · His jealousy exposes insecurity · Duchess: innocent, warm, easily
  • pleased, appreciative of life · "I gave commands; then all smiles stopped" — implied abuse of
  • power · Silent listener (envoy) and the marriage negotiation · Irony: the Duke condemns
  • himself while boasting · Neptune statue — control and possession · Patriarchal values;
  • themes of power, art and objectification · (CO3)
